Why New Braunfels businesses miss calls

New Braunfels sits on I-35 between San Antonio and Austin, with the Comal and Guadalupe rivers and Schlitterbahn drawing summer crowds. Food and hospitality employ over 10% of workers, while new neighborhoods keep builders and home services busy. A river outfitter, a restaurant and a plumber may all see their phones ring hardest on the same hot weekend, when they have the fewest people free.

Which New Braunfels businesses benefit most?

  • Restaurants: Answer visitors’ repeat questions during peak season.
  • HVAC and contractors: New homes and summer heat bring steady calls.
  • Real estate agents: Buyers moving between Austin and San Antonio call at all hours.

AI receptionist: Gives your hours, takes the group details and passes them to your manager.

Can you keep your New Braunfels phone number?

Yes. New Braunfels callers will usually see the 830 and 726 area codes, and you can keep the number customers already know. Forward it to the AI for all calls, only after hours, or only when your team does not pick up. We can also set up a new local number. Everything is set up remotely, so you do not need new equipment or a visit to an office.

What to check before you go live

  1. Test real calls: ask awkward questions, not only easy ones, and listen to how it handles them.
  2. Set the rules: decide which calls transfer to a person and which become messages.
  3. Plan your minutes: estimate your busiest month, not an average one.
  4. Tell callers what you need to: Texas is generally treated as a one-party consent state for recording calls, but rules differ for callers in other states, so check with your advisor if you record calls.
